speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a complex medical history with gait and limb ataxia; to narrow this down, can you tell me if your symptoms started suddenly or gradually, and do you experience any vertigo or double vision? Also, have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunk" appearance suggests cerebellar involvement; have you noticed any slurred speech, trouble swallowing, or a change in your handwriting? Additionally, given your significant medical history, is there a chance you have a history of alcohol use disorder or prior stroke?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of uncontrolled Crohn's disease, natalizumab use, and cerebellar ataxia strongly suggests Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Did you experience any memory changes, personality shifts, or visual disturbances like blind spots alongside these motor symptoms? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in the context of uncontrolled Crohn's disease.
